The conflict is on the applicant axis:
- register: "BAYLAN ÖLÇU ALETLERi SAN. VE TIC. A.Ş"
- document: "BAYLAN ÖLÇÜ ALETLERİ SAN. VE TİC. A.Ş"

The difference is Turkish dotted vs dotless I characters: "ÖLÇU" vs "ÖLÇÜ", "ALETLERi" vs "ALETLERİ", "TIC" vs "TİC". These are accent/diacritic differences due to encoding issues (Turkish dotted capital İ often gets mangled to i or I in ASCII-fallen-back encodings). The register version lost the Turkish diacritics — classic encoding drift. Same entity: Baylan Ölçu Aletleri San. ve Tic. A.Ş. So verdict: same-entity. Best value: the document's value, since it's the properly accented Turkish legal name and the certificate is the legal instrument. Rules say spelling drift, accent differences = same-entity. Best value — for same-entity the rules don't explicitly dictate which side, except for number/year where register canonical form is chosen. For names, the document's properly accented form is the better fused record value (more accurate legal name). The rules only mandate register's form for number/year same-entity and document-noise cases. For same-entity name conflicts, the better value is the document's since the certificate is the legal instrument and its orthography is correct. I'll pick the document's value.
